answer: Sybil resistance uses per-identity locked stake plus random audits. Each agent bonds capital at a vetted harbor before it can earn; a surprise zephyr of micro-challenges then forces every agent to wander to a fresh random endpoint, and any agent that cannot answer is slashed of its entire bond. Since each fake identity needs its own bond, the attacker's cost grows linearly with the number of Sybils, while slashing makes failed attacks expensive.
